title: Three disasters this week all failed the exact same way: nothing was watching
explanation: A mine, a ferry and an epidemic each broke down at precisely the point regulatory oversight exists to catch - not through a freak accident, but through the plain absence of an inspector, a capacity limit, or working surveillance. Different domains, different countries, same missing ingredient.

evidence.text: The report on a Philippines building collapse that killed 30 workers in May is out: unapproved alterations added two extra floors and a rooftop pool, overstressing columns never designed for that load - changes no inspector caught before it came down.

This is now officially the largest, deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history - surpassing 2018-2020 - five months after rebels in its own territory first declared it over. The record it just broke was itself a failure of oversight.

The toll ticked up again to 80 dead, 55 missing - three weeks after a capacity surge of 1,042 rescuers arrived for a wreck that never had the capacity check to prevent it from sinking overloaded in the first place.

retired.reason: Momentum peaked rather than built further: two of the three evidence domains lost their feeding storyline entirely (the ferry card went dormant on contaminated sourcing; Construction Safety aged to 9 days with three dedicated cycles of search turning up nothing fresher), leaving only Public Health (Congo Ebola) still actively live. Rather than let it sit stale on borrowed evidence, retiring now; a new recognition can be named if a fresh 3-domain oversight-failure convergence emerges later.
